source_snapshot.procedure: Power on, mount an ISO through BMC virtual media, install Linux with all packages, reboot, verify usability and inspect OS event logs; generic setup says clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: OS installation completes, the system works after reboot and event logs contain no unapproved error/fail/warning entries.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL posts InsertMedia to a fixed Redfish path using `curl -k` and HTTP media, then reads Image/Inserted. It proves neither secure media identity and transfer nor host attachment, safe disk selection, installation, reboot health, logs or eject cleanup.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL destructive risk correctly requires vendor endpoint discovery, trusted ISO, designated disposable disk, console installation proof, post-reboot checks and mandatory media/boot cleanup.

old_problem: A successful InsertMedia response is only the management-plane request. The source's real coverage includes ISO attachment, firmware selection, destructive full Linux installation, all-packages completion, reboot usability, log acceptance and cleanup; the supplied command guesses the endpoint, disables TLS trust and leaves the target disk and package/log criteria undefined.
disposition_reason: Retain the complete attach→host visibility→one-time boot→approved disk install→all-packages verification→reboot health/log review→eject/clear chain. The Review-layer case supplies explicit proof and stop gates while the Project binds the vendor media resource, immutable ISO, disposable disk, install/package recipe and known-event allowlist. Those runtime values do not require another engineering classification decision, but no destructive install is executable until they are supplied and approved.
decision_basis: XLSX row 916, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, related operations context and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.
Virtual-media request acceptance, BMC media transfer, host device visibility, firmware boot selection and completed OS installation are separate evidence layers; none implies the next.
The source explicitly includes Linux with all packages, reboot usability and event-log acceptance, so a mount-only result would unlawfully reduce coverage.
Disk identity, immutable ISO, Project package manifest and pinned known-event allowlist can be bound safely as execution prerequisites without guessing or keeping the engineering decision Pending.

test_case.test_name: Secure BMC virtual-media Linux installation, reboot validation and cleanup
test_case.purpose: Verify the selected BMC virtual-media implementation securely attaches the approved immutable Linux ISO to the correct SUT, boots it once, installs the Project-defined complete package profile only to the designated disposable disk, returns a usable OS after reboot, satisfies event-log acceptance and fully ejects media/clears temporary boot state.
required_package: BMC/SUT/BIOS/storage identity plus vendor-discovered VirtualMedia instance, Insert/Eject actions, supported transport and connection-state fields
Immutable approved ISO URL, version/architecture, hash/signature, authenticated BMC-reachable TLS transport and trust chain
Exact disposable target disk identity/topology/capacity with proof it is not an OS/boot/EFI/mounted/swap/LVM/RAID/device-mapper or unknown protected device
Project OS edition, boot mode, partitioning, driver/repository and complete `all packages` manifest with expected verification output
Separate media-attach, one-time boot/power and destructive-install approvals with KVM/SOL/local recovery
Post-install OS/device/service acceptance and pinned event-log known-message allowlist, plus eject/override-clear final-state plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL DESTRUCTIVE WORKFLOW; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT EACH APPROVAL. Preserve logs, discover the actual vendor VirtualMedia resource/actions, verify TLS/authentication and immutable ISO hash/signature, and prove the exact disposable disk while excluding every protected/unknown device. After attach approval, insert once and verify transfer, connected state, BMC audit and host media visibility. Obtain separate boot/power approval, set only an approved one-time media boot, and prove firmware selects that ISO. At the installer boundary, re-display target disk and obtain destructive-install approval; install the Project partition/package profile through KVM/SOL with complete console evidence. Verify package manifest, OS/device/service health and logs after reboot, then eject media, clear the temporary override and prove no out-of-scope storage changed. Never use guessed paths, `-k`, mutable unauthenticated HTTP, auto-retry or auto-reinstall.
test_case.expected_result: The exact approved ISO is securely transferred, connected and visible to the intended host; one-time firmware boot selects it; the Project install profile and every required package complete on only the designated disk; the installed OS reboots to a usable state with expected devices/services and only allowlisted event entries. Virtual media is then disconnected/ejected, the one-time override is clear, persistent boot order is unchanged and all out-of-scope storage is untouched.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the full evidence chain: discovered supported endpoint, verified image/trust, connected host media, actual media boot, exact safe disk, successful Project package manifest, usable post-reboot OS/device/service state, logs reconciled to a pinned allowlist, and eject/boot cleanup. HTTP success or Image/Inserted alone cannot pass. Wrong media/host/disk, checksum/transfer error, installer warning, missing package/device, unapproved log, failed reboot or cleanup failure is FAIL and stops without retry. Missing image, disk, recipe, allowlist, approval or recovery is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Do not clear BMC/SEL, existing OS, installer, storage or audit evidence; preserve the complete baseline and first failure.
Never guess manager/media indices, expose credentials, disable TLS verification or use mutable/untrusted installation media.
Never infer a safe disk. Positively identify the disposable target and exclude OS/boot/EFI/mounted/swap/LVM/RAID/device-mapper and unknown devices before approval.
Obtain distinct approval for attach, boot/power and destructive partition/install boundaries; do not automate past a missing confirmation.
Stop on any identity, transfer, boot, disk, installer, device, log or cleanup mismatch; do not automatically retry download, boot, partition or installation.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/storage identity, protected-device map, Project install/package recipe, destructive approvals and preserved pre-test logs
Discovered VirtualMedia resource/actions, TLS/auth method, immutable ISO version/hash/signature and BMC reachability/transfer/connected/host-visibility proof
One-time boot flags and firmware/KVM evidence selecting the exact media without persistent-order change
Installer console evidence naming the exact disk, partition result, OS identity, drivers/repositories and complete required-package verification
Post-reboot OS Ready/usability, services, complete device/storage/network inventory and event-log reconciliation to the pinned allowlist
Media eject/disconnect, override clear, unchanged out-of-scope storage, recovery disposition, no-retry proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong media, boot path or disk, checksum/transfer/installer failure, unexpected device/log result or reboot/cleanup failure, halt all later destructive actions and preserve BMC, console, installer and storage evidence. Detach media only when safe and use the pre-approved local/console recovery or approved image restore for the designated test disk. Do not repartition, reboot or reinstall as an automatic retry; any recovery mutation needs fresh authorization.

source_conflict.reason: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require an end-to-end virtual-media OS installation. Undefined `all packages`, known events and zero machine-time are readiness/data-quality gaps, not contradictory purposes.

blocked.reason: The end-to-end method, proof points and safe recovery are defined. Vendor endpoint, image, disk, install recipe and allowlist are Project execution inputs, so the engineering review can resolve without claiming readiness.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Vendor media endpoint/actions; trusted ISO and transport; disposable disk; OS/partition/package recipe; known-event allowlist; separate approvals, recovery and cleanup state.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; CRITICAL DESTRUCTIVE OS INSTALLATION; MULTIPLE POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVALS REQUIRED; NO MEDIA, BOOT OR INSTALL ACTION EXECUTED

project_authority: BMC vendor VirtualMedia documentation, Project deployment/package recipe, approved storage map, PKI/media policy, event allowlist and recovery SOP define execution acceptance.
